# Decimal tabs in table cells — native controls

These original minimal OOXML fixtures are generated by `tools/cell_decimal_tabs_fixture.py`. No third-party template content or fonts are embedded. `mode12` and `mode15` use a fixed 240-point cell; their `-auto` counterparts use automatic layout and a 10-point preference. Each contains 30 cases.

native references were exported using the reference application. Cell-width records identify their source and PDF hashes and initialize native layout by exporting PDF before reading Cell.Width. `tools/record_cell_decimal_tabs.py` extracts text positions from those PDFs and binds the source, case manifest and reference PDF by SHA-256.

Observed behavior: with exactly one authored decimal tab stop, the reference application automatically aligns the initial cell field to it without an explicit tab. An explicit leading tab advances past that field. Multiple authored stops do not trigger automatic initial alignment. Hanging-indent stops do not count as a second authored stop. Automatic alignment does not paint a tab leader. Both compatibility modes show the same fixed-cell positions.

Candidate verification (not a claim of complete support): all 30 fixed cases in each mode match the recorded native reference text positions within 0.2 pt horizontally and 0.25 pt vertically. The modern fixed fixture passes editable open, no-edit package preservation, edit/unrelated-part preservation, exact undo, and reopen.

Outstanding: AutoFit intrinsic widths and narrow-cell wrapping. The candidate currently rejects several automatic-width controls, including plain initial decimal fields. The explicit multiple-stop minimum-width correction is independently covered by `autofit-explicit-decimal.spec.js`; cases 18 and 20 now match the reference application at 54.05 pt. Compatibility modes differ for some indented and leading-tab AutoFit controls. Do not mark this feature or any affected corpus template complete based on fixed-cell checks alone.
